evidence: This is supported by multiple citations (Calvet et al., 2020; Griffin and Allonby, 1979; Harrus et al., 1995; Savage et al., 2021).

claim: 1/148 sequestration in the brain causes more damage to the vasculature than IL3000.
source: Importantly, we showed that 1/148 sequestration in the brain causes more damage to the vasculature than IL3000 and that the parasite-endothelial cell interaction is longer-lived, thus corroborating the tropism of this strain to the brain vasculature.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the vascular permeability and sequestration duration data.

claim: The parasite-endothelial cell interaction is longer-lived in 1/148 infections than IL3000.
source: Importantly, we showed that 1/148 sequestration in the brain causes more damage to the vasculature than IL3000 and that the parasite-endothelial cell interaction is longer-lived, thus corroborating the tropism of this strain to the brain vasculature.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the sequestration duration data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: T. congolense 1/148 infection in C57BL/6 J mice is a good model of acute cerebral trypanosomiasis.
source: The analysis described so far comparing IL3000 and 1/148 strains clearly indicates that T. congolense 1/148 infection in C57BL/6 J mice is a good model of acute cerebral trypanosomiasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparative analysis of the two strains.

claim: T. congolense 1/148 infection resulted in downregulation of 588 genes in brain endothelial cells.
source: We compared the expression profiles of brain endothelial cells of mice non-infected and infected with T. congolense 1/148 and found that infection resulted in downregulation of 588 genes and upregulation of 612 genes (Figure 3B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: T. congolense 1/148 infection resulted in upregulation of 612 genes in brain endothelial cells.
source: We compared the expression profiles of brain endothelial cells of mice non-infected and infected with T. congolense 1/148 and found that infection resulted in downregulation of 588 genes and upregulation of 612 genes (Figure 3B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Within the 20 most upregulated transcripts in brain endothelial cells upon 1/148 infection, several genes are involved in the immune response, particularly those related to type 1 immunity.
source: Within the 20 most upregulated transcripts, we detected several genes involved in the immune response, and in particular those related to type 1 immunity (i.e. CXCL10, CXCL9, Basic leucine zipper transcription factor (Batf2), Growth differentiation factor 15 (Gdf15), CD300-like family member F (CD300lf), Z-DNA binding protein 1 (Zbp1), and guanylate-binding protein 10 (Gbp10)).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Within the 20 most upregulated transcripts in brain endothelial cells upon 1/148 infection, transcripts involved in angiogenesis, endothelial transmigration, and response to blood-brain-barrier dysfunction were detected.
source: We also detected transcripts involved in angiogenesis, endothelial transmigration, and in the response to blood-brain-barrier dysfunction, including amyloid precursor protein (APP), stanniocalcin 1 (Stc1), serine peptidase inhibitor (Serpina3f), syntenin 2 (Sdcbp2), angiopoietin 2 (Angpt2), and placental growth factor (Pgf) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 63% of the enriched gene sets in brain endothelial cells upon 1/148 infection related to inflammatory responses.
source: Results were consistent with the signature we observed from the most upregulated genes, as 63% of the enriched gene sets related to inflammatory responses (e.g. response to interferon gamma, positive regulation of defense response, response to tumor necrosis factor, cytokine-mediated signaling pathway, regulation of innate immune response, response to virus, response to interleukin-1, antigen processing and presentation, regulation of inflammatory response, leukocyte migration, etc.), and 7% to angiogenesis (e.g. angiogenesis, regeneration) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 7% of the enriched gene sets in brain endothelial cells upon 1/148 infection related to angiogenesis.
source: Results were consistent with the signature we observed from the most upregulated genes, as 63% of the enriched gene sets related to inflammatory responses (e.g. response to interferon gamma, positive regulation of defense response, response to tumor necrosis factor, cytokine-mediated signaling pathway, regulation of innate immune response, response to virus, response to interleukin-1, antigen processing and presentation, regulation of inflammatory response, leukocyte migration, etc.), and 7% to angiogenesis (e.g. angiogenesis, regeneration) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: T. congolense 1/148 infection results in endothelial activation.
source: These results show that T. congolense 1/148 infection results in endothelial activation, which is consistent with previous results (Ammar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression data and cited from Ammar et al., 2013.

claim: An activated endothelium upregulates the expression of integrin ligands which control the immune response.
source: So, and given that an activated endothelium upregulates the expression of integrin ligands which control the immune response (Lawson and Wolf, 2009), we also assessed the expression changes of intercellular adhesion molecule (ICAM) 1, ICAM2, and vascular cell adhesion molecule (VCAM) 1, three integrin ligands involved in leukocyte transendothelial migration.
evidence: This is cited from Lawson and Wolf, 2009.

claim: ICAM1, ICAM2, and VCAM1 are three integrin ligands involved in leukocyte transendothelial migration.
source: So, and given that an activated endothelium upregulates the expression of integrin ligands which control the immune response (Lawson and Wolf, 2009), we also assessed the expression changes of intercellular adhesion molecule (ICAM) 1, ICAM2, and vascular cell adhesion molecule (VCAM) 1, three integrin ligands involved in leukocyte transendothelial migration.
evidence: This is general knowledge about these molecules.

claim: ICAM1 was highly expressed in immune cells during T. congolense infection.
source: ICAM1 was highly expressed in immune cells (yellow arrowheads, Figure 3E), but also detectable in vessel walls (cyan arrowheads, Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ICAM1 was detectable in vessel walls during T. congolense infection.
source: ICAM1 was highly expressed in immune cells (yellow arrowheads, Figure 3E), but also detectable in vessel walls (cyan arrowheads, Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ICAM1 expression increased in the endothelium of the brain during 1/148 infection.
source: Consistent with the endothelium ribosome profiling data (which revealed ICAM1 to be upregulated upon 1/148 infection (FC = 1.62), but not of ICAM2 or VCAM1), we observed increased expression of ICAM1 in the endothelium of the brain (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value = 0.0312), but not of ICAM2, nor VCAM1 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: ICAM2 expression did not increase in the endothelium of the brain during 1/148 infection.
source: Consistent with the endothelium ribosome profiling data (which revealed ICAM1 to be upregulated upon 1/148 infection (FC = 1.62), but not of ICAM2 or VCAM1), we observed increased expression of ICAM1 in the endothelium of the brain (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value = 0.0312), but not of ICAM2, nor VCAM1 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: VCAM1 expression did not increase in the endothelium of the brain during 1/148 infection.
source: Consistent with the endothelium ribosome profiling data (which revealed ICAM1 to be upregulated upon 1/148 infection (FC = 1.62), but not of ICAM2 or VCAM1), we observed increased expression of ICAM1 in the endothelium of the brain (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value = 0.0312), but not of ICAM2, nor VCAM1 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: ICAM1 expression increased in the endothelium of the brain during IL3000 infection.
source: In IL3000 infections, we also observed an increase in ICAM1 expression by endothelial cells (p-value = 0.003).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: During 1/148 infections, ICAM1 increased in the lungs, heart, and liver.
source: During 1/148 infections, we observed ICAM1 also increased in the lungs, heart, and liver (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.01), whereas ICAM2 expression increased in the heart and kidneys (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.0001), and VCAM1 in the liver, spleen, and kidneys (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.01) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A, left).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: During 1/148 infections, ICAM2 expression increased in the heart and kidneys.
source: During 1/148 infections, we observed ICAM1 also increased in the lungs, heart, and liver (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.01), whereas ICAM2 expression increased in the heart and kidneys (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.0001), and VCAM1 in the liver, spleen, and kidneys (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.01) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A, left).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: During 1/148 infections, VCAM1 increased in the liver, spleen, and kidneys.
source: During 1/148 infections, we observed ICAM1 also increased in the lungs, heart, and liver (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.01), whereas ICAM2 expression increased in the heart and kidneys (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.0001), and VCAM1 in the liver, spleen, and kidneys (unpaired t-test with Welch's correction, p-value < 0.01) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A, left).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: During IL3000 infections, increased ICAM1 expression was not observed in organs other than the brain.
source: During IL3000 infections, we did not observe increased ICAM1 expression in remaining organs (Figure S2A, right).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Leukocytes expressed increased ICAM1 (fivefold) upon infection with either T. congolense strain.
source: Furthermore, we observed that leukocytes also expressed increased ICAM1 (fivefold) and ICAM2 (twofold), but not VCAM1, upon infection with either strain.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: Leukocytes expressed increased ICAM2 (twofold) upon infection with either T. congolense strain.
source: Furthermore, we observed that leukocytes also expressed increased ICAM1 (fivefold) and ICAM2 (twofold), but not VCAM1, upon infection with either strain.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: Leukocytes did not express increased VCAM1 upon infection with either T. congolense strain.
source: Furthermore, we observed that leukocytes also expressed increased ICAM1 (fivefold) and ICAM2 (twofold), but not VCAM1, upon infection with either strain.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: During 1/148 infections, expression of ICAM1 increased in all anatomic regions of the brain, with the exception of the hypothalamus.
source: We observed that, during 1/148 infections, expression of ICAM1 increased in all anatomic regions of the brain, with the exception of the hypothalamus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: During IL3000 infections, ICAM1 expression increased in all brain regions with the exception of the hippocampus, hypothalamus, and medulla.
source: In contrast, during IL3000 infections, ICAM1 expression increased in all brain regions with the exception of the hippocampus, hypothalamus, and medulla.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Parasite sequestration remains even throughout brain despite variations in endothelial ICAM1 expression, suggesting that ICAM1 is not the sole receptor for parasite cytoadhesion.
source: Given that parasite sequestration remains even throughout brain despite variations in endothelial ICAM1 expression suggests that ICAM1 is not the sole receptor for parasite cytoadhesion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of parasite sequestration and ICAM1 expression patterns.

claim: Endothelial cells respond to T. congolense infection by displaying a pro-inflammatory response.
source: In summary, analysis of the brain vasculature revealed that endothelial cells respond to T. congolense infection by displaying a pro-inflammatory response.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression and protein expression data.

claim: A significant increase in the levels of CXCL9 was confirmed at days 3 and 6 p.i. during both 1/148 and IL3000 infections.
source: We confirmed a significant increase in the levels of CXCL9 and CXCL10 at days 3 and 6 p.i., during both 1/148 and IL3000 infections, compared to the non-infected control (twoway ANOVA, CXCL9: p-value < 0.0091 and=0.0107, respectively; CXCL10: p-value = 0.0013 and 0.0082; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A significant increase in the levels of CXCL10 was confirmed at days 3 and 6 p.i. during both 1/148 and IL3000 infections.
source: We confirmed a significant increase in the levels of CXCL9 and CXCL10 at days 3 and 6 p.i., during both 1/148 and IL3000 infections, compared to the non-infected control (twoway ANOVA, CXCL9: p-value < 0.0091 and=0.0107, respectively; CXCL10: p-value = 0.0013 and 0.0082; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The levels of TNFα show a tendency to increase with infection in both T. congolense strains.
source: The levels of TNFα show a tendency to increase with infection in both strains.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The levels of IFNγ only show an ascending trend during 1/148 infections.
source: However, the levels of IFNγ only show an ascending trend during 1/148 infections.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A systemic pro-inflammatory response is present in the first week of infection with both T. congolense strains.
source: These results support the presence of a systemic pro-inflammatory response in the first week of infection with both strains of T. congolense.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cytokine profiling data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The number of ICAM1+ monocytes in the blood during 1/148 infections increased 25-fold compared to the non-infected control.
source: We observed that the number of ICAM1+ monocytes in the blood during 1/148 infections increased 25-fold compared to the non-infected control and 4-fold compared to IL3000 infections (two-way ANOVA with Tukey's Multiple Comparison Test, p-value = 0.0002 and 0.0131) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The number of ICAM1+ monocytes in the blood during 1/148 infections increased 4-fold compared to IL3000 infections.
source: We observed that the number of ICAM1+ monocytes in the blood during 1/148 infections increased 25-fold compared to the non-infected control and 4-fold compared to IL3000 infections (two-way ANOVA with Tukey's Multiple Comparison Test, p-value = 0.0002 and 0.0131) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: There was an increase in the number of both extravascular and intravascular CD45+ cells upon 1/148 infection.
source: We found an increase in the number of both extravascular (unpaired t-test, p-value = 0.0482, t=2.813, df = 4) and intravascular (unpaired t-test, p-value = 0.0160, t=4.0007, df = 4) CD45+ cells upon 1/148 infection, but not upon IL3000 infection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the immune response is much stronger in the acute strain.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was no increase in the number of extravascular or intravascular CD45+ cells upon IL3000 infection.
source: We found an increase in the number of both extravascular (unpaired t-test, p-value = 0.0482, t=2.813, df = 4) and intravascular (unpaired t-test, p-value = 0.0160, t=4.0007, df = 4) CD45+ cells upon 1/148 infection, but not upon IL3000 infection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the immune response is much stronger in the acute strain.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The immune response is much stronger in the acute T. congolense strain 1/148 than in IL3000.
source: We found an increase in the number of both extravascular (unpaired t-test, p-value = 0.0482, t=2.813, df = 4) and intravascular (unpaired t-test, p-value = 0.0160, t=4.0007, df = 4) CD45+ cells upon 1/148 infection, but not upon IL3000 infection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the immune response is much stronger in the acute strain.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CD45+ cell data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The contribution of intravascular leukocytes to the total immune cells in the brain is higher in infected animals.
source: Additionally, the contribution of intravascular leukocytes to the total immune cells in the brain is higher in infected animals (14%±4 vs 25%±1).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: The number of intravascular CD11b+Ly6C-CD11c+ dendritic cells increased by fourfold in 1/148 infections only.
source: The number of intravascular CD11b+Ly6C-CD11c+ dendritic cells (DC) and CD11b+Ly6C+ monocytes increased by fourfold in 1/148 infections only (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0005, <0.0001, respectively) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The number of intravascular CD11b+Ly6C+ monocytes increased by fourfold in 1/148 infections only.
source: The number of intravascular CD11b+Ly6C-CD11c+ dendritic cells (DC) and CD11b+Ly6C+ monocytes increased by fourfold in 1/148 infections only (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0005, <0.0001, respectively) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 73% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 during 1/148 infection.
source: Importantly, 73% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 during 1/148 infection, compared to only 8% in the non-infected control and 32% in IL3000 infection, which is reflected in a significant increase (35-fold) in the number of ICAM1-expressing monocytes circulating in the brain vasculature (two-way ANOVA, p-value < 0.0001) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: 8% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 in the non-infected control.
source: Importantly, 73% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 during 1/148 infection, compared to only 8% in the non-infected control and 32% in IL3000 infection, which is reflected in a significant increase (35-fold) in the number of ICAM1-expressing monocytes circulating in the brain vasculature (two-way ANOVA, p-value < 0.0001) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: 32% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 in IL3000 infection.
source: Importantly, 73% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 during 1/148 infection, compared to only 8% in the non-infected control and 32% in IL3000 infection, which is reflected in a significant increase (35-fold) in the number of ICAM1-expressing monocytes circulating in the brain vasculature (two-way ANOVA, p-value < 0.0001) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: There was a significant increase (35-fold) in the number of ICAM1-expressing monocytes circulating in the brain vasculature during 1/148 infection.
source: Importantly, 73% of the intravascular monocytes expressed ICAM1 during 1/148 infection, compared to only 8% in the non-infected control and 32% in IL3000 infection, which is reflected in a significant increase (35-fold) in the number of ICAM1-expressing monocytes circulating in the brain vasculature (two-way ANOVA, p-value < 0.0001) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: IL3000-infected mice had increased numbers of extravascular B cells in the brain parenchyma.
source: In contrast, the number of extravascular lymphoid cells present in the brain changed differently depending on the strain. IL3000-infected mice had increased numbers of extravascular B cells in the brain parenchyma (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0341), whereas in the 1/148 infection, T helper cells (CD4+) were increased by twofold (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0.0305; Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: In 1/148 infection, T helper cells (CD4+) were increased by twofold in the brain parenchyma.
source: In contrast, the number of extravascular lymphoid cells present in the brain changed differently depending on the strain. IL3000-infected mice had increased numbers of extravascular B cells in the brain parenchyma (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0341), whereas in the 1/148 infection, T helper cells (CD4+) were increased by twofold (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0.0305; Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Intravascular cytotoxic T cells (CD8+) expressing ICAM1 were increased in 1/148 infections.
source: In terms of ICAM1 expression, intravascular cytotoxic T cells (CD8+) were increased in 1/148 infections (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0120) and extravascular ICAM1+ B cells were increased in IL3000 infections (two-way ANOVA, p-value < 0.0001) (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Extravascular ICAM1+ B cells were increased in IL3000 infections.
source: In terms of ICAM1 expression, intravascular cytotoxic T cells (CD8+) were increased in 1/148 infections (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0120) and extravascular ICAM1+ B cells were increased in IL3000 infections (two-way ANOVA, p-value < 0.0001) (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: The development of cerebral trypanosomiasis is associated with the recruitment of inflammatory monocytes to the brain vasculature, most of which express ICAM1.
source: Overall, these data show that, upon infection, the development of cerebral trypanosomiasis is associated with the recruitment of inflammatory monocytes to the brain vasculature, most of which express ICAM1 (Figure 4E), and the infiltration of CD4+ T cells into the brain parenchyma (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the immune cell profiling data shown in Figures 4E and 4I.

claim: The development of cerebral trypanosomiasis is associated with the infiltration of CD4+ T cells into the brain parenchyma.
source: Overall, these data show that, upon infection, the development of cerebral trypanosomiasis is associated with the recruitment of inflammatory monocytes to the brain vasculature, most of which express ICAM1 (Figure 4E), and the infiltration of CD4+ T cells into the brain parenchyma (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the immune cell profiling data shown in Figures 4E and 4I.

claim: α-ICAM1-treated mice showed fewer signs of cerebral disease than isotype-treated controls.
source: We noticed that α-ICAM1-treated mice showed fewer signs of cerebral disease, so we used SHIRPA (i.e. SmithKline Beecham, Harwell, Imperial College, Royal London Hospital, phenotype assessment), a mouse phenotypic assessment protocol (Rogers et al., 1997), to test whether α-ICAM1-treated mice were neurologically fitter than isotype-treated controls.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental observations.

claim: Mice infected with T. congolense strain 1/148 showed defects in posture, velocity of escape upon touching, positional passivity, type of locomotion, and grip strength on day 6 post-infection.
source: Mice infected with the strain 1/148 showed defects in all these parameters on day 6 post-infection (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The alterations observed in mice infected with T. congolense 1/148 are consistent with the changes described in dogs infected with T. congolense.
source: These alterations are consistent with the changes described in dogs infected with T. congolense (Harrus et al., 1995), showing that SHIRPA protocol is a useful quantitative method to score neurological alterations associated with cerebral trypanosomiasis in this mouse model.
evidence: This is cited from Harrus et al., 1995.

claim: SHIRPA protocol is a useful quantitative method to score neurological alterations associated with cerebral trypanosomiasis in this mouse model.
source: These alterations are consistent with the changes described in dogs infected with T. congolense (Harrus et al., 1995), showing that SHIRPA protocol is a useful quantitative method to score neurological alterations associated with cerebral trypanosomiasis in this mouse model.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the SHIRPA test results.

claim: α-ICAM1-treated mice performed better than the control group in all parameters relating to neurological impairment.
source: The SHIRPA protocol revealed that α-ICAM1-treated mice performed better than the control group in all parameters relating to neurological impairment, and particularly those relating to movement and strength (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: α-ICAM1-treated mice survived longer than isotype-treated controls, as 50% of the mice were still alive at day 20 p.i.
source: Importantly, we also found that α-ICAM1-treated mice survived longer than isotype-treated controls, as 50% of the mice were still alive at day 20 p.i, when the experiment was terminated (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Brain necropsy showed reduced neuropathology in α-ICAM1-treated mice.
source: Brain necropsy also showed reduced neuropathology (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Total parasite load in the brain was unaffected by α-ICAM1 treatment.
source: We found that total parasite load was unaffected by treatment (Figure 5E, left), but the percentage of sequestered parasites was reduced by 44% (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0025) (Figure 5E, right).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The percentage of sequestered parasites in the brain was reduced by 44% by α-ICAM1 treatment.
source: We found that total parasite load was unaffected by treatment (Figure 5E, left), but the percentage of sequestered parasites was reduced by 44% (two-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0025) (Figure 5E, right).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: T. congolense 1/148 parasites bound equally efficiently to recombinant ICAM1 protein, to BSA or recombinant CD36 protein in static conditions.
source: Parasites bound equally efficiently to recombinant ICAM1 protein, to BSA or recombinant CD36 protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: T. congolense 1/148 parasite sequestration in static conditions is not enhanced by ICAM1 binding.
source: Whilst we cannot exclude the possibility that by collecting parasites from the blood, we are selecting those with lower sequestration capacity or lower affinity to ICAM1, these results suggest that T. congolense 1/148 parasite sequestration in static conditions is not enhanced by ICAM1 binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Blocking ICAM1 reduces parasite sequestration in the brain.
source: These data show that blocking ICAM1 reduces parasite sequestration in the brain, improves cerebral trypanosomiasis severity and promotes mouse survival, but this effect appears to be independent of direct parasite binding to the ICAM1 receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ICAM1 blocking experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Blocking ICAM1 improves cerebral trypanosomiasis severity.
source: These data show that blocking ICAM1 reduces parasite sequestration in the brain, improves cerebral trypanosomiasis severity and promotes mouse survival, but this effect appears to be independent of direct parasite binding to the ICAM1 receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ICAM1 blocking experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Blocking ICAM1 promotes mouse survival.
source: These data show that blocking ICAM1 reduces parasite sequestration in the brain, improves cerebral trypanosomiasis severity and promotes mouse survival, but this effect appears to be independent of direct parasite binding to the ICAM1 receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ICAM1 blocking experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The effect of ICAM1 blocking appears to be independent of direct parasite binding to the ICAM1 receptor.
source: These data show that blocking ICAM1 reduces parasite sequestration in the brain, improves cerebral trypanosomiasis severity and promotes mouse survival, but this effect appears to be independent of direct parasite binding to the ICAM1 receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro binding assay and in vivo blocking experiments.

claim: ICAM1 is important in leukocyte recruitment and infiltration.
source: Given that ICAM1 is important in leukocyte recruitment and infiltration (Lawson and Wolf, 2009), next we investigated whether the phenotypic effect of ICAM1 blocking could derive from an impaired immunological response.
evidence: This is cited from Lawson and Wolf, 2009.

claim: ICAM1 blocking resulted in a 67% ± 5% reduction in the number of circulating nucleated cells in the brain vasculature.
source: By intravital imaging, we detected a 67% ± 5% reduction in the number of circulating nucleated cells (assumed to be leukocytes due to their size and complexity; one-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0270), which was not observed when blocking either ICAM2 or VCAM1 (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: The reduction in circulating nucleated cells in the brain vasculature was not observed when blocking either ICAM2 or VCAM1.
source: By intravital imaging, we detected a 67% ± 5% reduction in the number of circulating nucleated cells (assumed to be leukocytes due to their size and complexity; one-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.0270), which was not observed when blocking either ICAM2 or VCAM1 (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: ICAM1 blocking may improve disease outcome by reducing parasite sequestration and the magnitude of the immune response.
source: Overall, these results indicate that the ICAM1 blocking may improve disease outcome by reducing parasite sequestration and the magnitude of the immune response.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ICAM1 blocking experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Mice treated with clodronate liposomes showed high peripheral parasitemia earlier than mice receiving either PBS-filled liposomes or PBS only.
source: We observed that mice treated with clodronate liposomes showed high peripheral parasitemia earlier than mice receiving either PBS-filled liposomes or PBS only (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mice receiving clodronate liposomes died between days 6 and 7.
source: Mice receiving clodronate liposomes died between days 6 and 7, compared to days 7–8 when receiving control liposomes, and days 7–10 if only PBS was administered (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Monocyte/macrophage depletion increased severity of neurological impairment.
source: Moreover, we performed mouse behavioral assessment on day 6 post-infection and observed that monocyte/macrophage depletion increased severity of neurological impairment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
